summary: Robert Deliège is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford from around 1977 to 1981. He held positions at the University of Kerala and as a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain around 1989.
Robert Duquenne is a specialist in Tantric Buddhism working in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, Robert E. Morrell studied under teacher William H. McCullough and doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower. He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis (attested in 1985 and 2006).

Active in Indology, Robert E. Svoboda studied at the University of Oklahoma (circa 1970–1972) and under his mentor Vimalananda (circa 1975–1983). By 2008, he held adjunct positions at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Robert F. Rhodes is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who pursued a Ph.D. at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997 and 2012–2014) and was a committee member for the Otani Academic Society in 2000.

Robert Florida works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University, and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He served as a professor at Indiana University from around 1989 to 2006 and held an appointment at Vanderbilt University around 2010.

Robert Gardner earned a BA from Harvard University (circa 1943–1947), assisted Thomas Whittemore at the Fogg Museum (circa 1947–1949), and taught at the University of Puget Sound (circa 1950–1953) before serving as a professor at Harvard University (1956–1997).

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1900 to 1908 and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

Robert Göbl was a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and subsequently held a post there from around 1955 to 1989.

Japanology scholar Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard (BA circa 1940–1944) and the University of Michigan (MA circa 1945–1947). He taught at Minnesota, Stanford, directed the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired Far Eastern Languages at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley, where he became D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor around 2003.

Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (circa 1941–1947) and Balliol College, Oxford (circa 1948–1950). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from around 1950 to 1994.
Robert Hyde Colebrooke worked in history and archaeology. He was a member of The Asiatic Society from 1785 to 1802 and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1794 to 1808.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1955 to 1988 and held a professorship at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini by 1995. He held posts at UC Berkeley and Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh. In 1787, he founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and taught Buddhist Studies at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at Tartu and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Tallinn Cathedral School, University of Breslau, Austrian Academy of Sciences, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1968–1976), specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held professorships at the University of Arizona (~1981–2020) and Harvard University (~2002–2006).
